title: Reaching and signing in to the ZCC API: OneAPI gateway and legacy login

prose.text: The ZCC API is reached two ways: through the OneAPI gateway with a bearer token, or through the legacy Mobile Admin Portal login with an API key and secret. This subject records where each path lives and how its token is presented.

prose.label: OneAPI path.
prose.text: {{oneapi-base-url}} [[shared.sdk-python.client-configuration:bearer-header]] The OneAPI credential variables and token endpoint are common to the Python SDK: [[zia.sdk-python.authentication:oneapi-env-vars]], [[zia.sdk-python.authentication:vanity-domain-token-url]]. Which roles or scopes an API client needs for ZCC is open {{gap:oneapi-zcc-scopes}}.
{{legacy-auth-token-header}} The legacy host differs between the help article and the SDKs {{divergence:legacy-host}}.
In the Go SDK's legacy mode, some ZCC calls are sent through the ZIA client: [[zcc.sdk-go.legacy-routing]].

checks.do: Whether the ZCC API has been enabled for the organization before treating a failed first call as a credential problem.
Whether a hand-built legacy call sent the JWT in an `auth-token` header rather than as an Authorization bearer token.
Which host a legacy script logs in to, against the api-mobile or mobile hostnames the sources give.

api-must-be-enabled.statement: Availability of the Zscaler Client Connector API is limited: the organization must have it enabled by contacting Zscaler Support or the account team, and must add an API key, before using it.

quotes: Availability of the Zscaler Client Connector API is limited. To enable the API for your organization, contact the Zscaler Account team.
You must enable the API for your organization. To enable the API, contact Zscaler Support or submit a Zscaler Support ticket.

oneapi-base-url.statement: On the OneAPI path the ZCC API is served from the gateway host `https://api.zsapi.net` under `/zcc/papi/public/v1`: the captured contract's server is `https://api.zsapi.net/zcc` with paths under `/papi/public/v1`, and the Python SDK's default base URL is `https://api.zsapi.net` with ZCC endpoints prefixed `/zcc/papi/public/v1`.

quotes: BASE_URL = "https://api.zsapi.net"  # Default base URL for API calls

oneapi-base-url.conditions: The Python SDK resolves other gateway hosts for non-production and government clouds; this claim is about the default commercial gateway.

legacy-login-request.statement: The legacy API is signed in to with a POST to `/papi/auth/v1/login` carrying `apiKey` and `secretKey`; the response's `jwtToken` is the token passed on subsequent calls.

quotes: Send a POST request to the /login endpoint with the following parameters:
The authorization token is passed onto subsequent calls for authentication.

url = "https://mobile.<cloudName>.net/papi/auth/v1/login" payload={"apiKey":"{apiKey}","secretKey":"{secretKey}"} headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } response = requests.request("POST", url, headers=headers, json=payload)
apiKey: A string that contains the API client ID.
secretKey: A string that contains the client secret.
you must retrieve your authorization token (JWT Token<jwtToken>)

legacy-token-expiry.statement: The legacy authentication token expires after 3600 seconds (one hour) by default.

quotes: The authentication token expiry time is set to 3600 seconds (one hour) by default.

legacy-secret-shown-once.statement: The client secret of a legacy API key can be copied only in the Client Connector Portal when the key is first created.

quotes: The client secret (i.e., secret key) is only accessible within the Zscaler Client Connector Portal when the API key is created for the first time.
The client secret is only available to copy when adding an API key.

legacy-auth-token-header.statement: On the legacy path the JWT is sent in an `auth-token` request header, not as an Authorization bearer token: the help article's example uses `auth-token`, and both SDKs' legacy ZCC clients set that header.

quotes: // Legacy struct holds and instance of each legacy API client to support backwards compatibility

legacy-host.summary: Which host serves the legacy login and API: the help article uses `mobile.<cloudName>.net`, while both SDKs use `api-mobile.<cloud>.net` (Python maps the zscalerten cloud to `mobile6`).

positions.says: The help article's sign-in example posts to `https://mobile.<cloudName>.net/papi/auth/v1/login`.
The Python legacy client builds `https://api-mobile.<cloud>.net` and logs in at `/papi/auth/v1/login`, except that the zscalerten cloud uses the `mobile6` subdomain.
The Go legacy client builds `https://api-mobile.<cloud>.net/papi` and logs in at `/auth/v1/login` under it.

legacy-host.impact: A legacy script built from the help article targets a different hostname from the SDKs. Which of `mobile` and `api-mobile` a given cloud answers on, and whether the OneAPI gateway, under which the captured contract lists every operation, accepts the legacy login, is not settled by these sources.

oneapi-zcc-scopes.title: What an OneAPI client needs to call the ZCC API
oneapi-zcc-scopes.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the ZCC portal API requires a tenant admin session, and API client credentials need ZCC scopes (`zcc.*`). No captured source names the ZIdentity role or scopes an API client needs for ZCC endpoints. The contract names a requirement for one endpoint only: `getCompanyInfo` is allowed for a OneAPI caller or a token with admin or read-only admin privileges ([[zcc.api.company-wire:company-read-access]]).
oneapi-zcc-scopes.blocks: telling a 401 or 403 on a OneAPI ZCC call apart from a missing grant
